title: Visiting and being invited
goal: Accept and decline invitations, behave as a guest, and use hospitality phrases that have no real equivalent in English.
bekal: compliment the host's food and home the right way

dialogs.title: حِوَار — عَشَاءٌ فِي بَيْتِ لَيْلَى
dialogs.intro: Budi is invited to dinner at Laila's family home.

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.baca: ahlan wa sahlan! tafaḍḍal, al-baitu baituk.
lines.id: Welcome! Come in, make yourself at home.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: شُكْرًا. هٰذِهِ هَدِيَّةٌ بَسِيطَةٌ مِنْ إِنْدُونِيسِيَا.
lines.baca: shukran. haadhihi hadiyyatun basiiṭatun min Induuniisiyaa.
lines.id: Thank you. Here's a little something from Indonesia.
lines.literal: thanks. this gift simple from Indonesia.

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.text: مَا كَانَ يَجِبُ! شُكْرًا يَا بُنَيَّ. تَفَضَّلْ بِالْجُلُوسِ.
lines.baca: maa kaana yajib! shukran yaa bunayya. tafaḍḍal bil-juluus.
lines.id: You shouldn't have! Thank you, son. Please, sit down.
lines.literal: not was necessary! thanks O my-little-son. please with-sitting.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا، مَا شَاءَ اللهُ.
lines.literal: house-your(pl.) beautiful very, what willed God.

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.text: اَللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ. اَلْعَشَاءُ جَاهِزٌ، تَفَضَّلُوا.
lines.baca: allaahu yubaariku fiik. al-'ashaa'u jaahiz, tafaḍḍaluu.
lines.id: God bless you. Dinner is ready, please come.
lines.literal: God blesses in-you. the-dinner ready, please(pl.).

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: It smells delicious! What did you cook?

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.text: مَحْشِي وَأَرُزٌّ بِاللَّحْمِ. كُلْ، لَا تَخْجَلْ!
lines.baca: mahshii wa aruzzun bil-lahm. kul, laa takhjal!
lines.id: Mahshi and rice with meat. Eat, don't be shy!
lines.literal: mahshi and rice with-the-meat. eat, don't you-be-shy!

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: Delicious! Thank you for the cooking.

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.text: خُذْ زِيَادَةً! أَنْتَ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ شَيْئًا.
lines.baca: khudh ziyaadah! anta lam ta'kul shai'an.
lines.id: Have some more! You haven't eaten anything.
lines.literal: take more! you not you-ate something.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: شَبِعْتُ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. كُلُّ شَيْءٍ كَانَ مُمْتَازًا.
lines.baca: shabi'tu, alhamdu lillaah. kullu shai'in kaana mumtaazan.
lines.id: I'm full, thank God. Everything was excellent.
lines.literal: I-am-full, praise be-to-God. every thing was excellent.

lines.speaker: أُمُّ لَيْلَى:
lines.text: بِالْهَنَاءِ وَالشِّفَاءِ. تَعَالَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، اَلْبَابُ مَفْتُوحٌ.
lines.baca: bil-hanaa'i wash-shifaa'. ta'aala marratan ukhraa, al-baabu maftuuh.
lines.id: Enjoy, and to your health. Come again, our door is always open.
lines.literal: with-pleasure and-healing. come time other, the-door open.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: جَزَاكِ اللهُ خَيْرًا. بِإِذْنِكُمْ، سَأَذْهَبُ الْآنَ.
lines.id: May God reward you. With your permission, I'll be going.
lines.literal: rewarded-you God goodness. with permission-your(pl.), will-I-go now.

notes: **اَلْبَيْتُ بَيْتُكَ — "the house is your house".** A standard welcome that isn't an empty figure of speech: guests really are treated that way. Equivalents: بَيْتُكَ, أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي بَيْتِنَا.
**مَا كَانَ يَجِبُ — "you shouldn't have".** Said when receiving a gift; it isn't a refusal but a courtesy. The gift is still accepted — just like the English phrase.
**يَا بُنَيَّ — an affectionate "my son".** A diminutive of اِبْن, used by older people to younger ones. To a girl: يَا بُنَيَّتِي. It signals warmth, not condescension.

**يَدَاكِ سَلِيمَتَانِ is literally "may your two hands be safe".** It's the standard compliment to whoever cooked, roughly "bless your hands". In the Levant you'll more often hear تِسْلَمْ إِيدَيْكِ. Saying it pleases the host far more than a mere لَذِيذ.
**كُلْ، لَا تَخْجَلْ — two imperative forms.** كُلْ (eat!) from أَكَلَ, and the prohibition لَا تَخْجَلْ (don't be shy). Notice that the command from أَكَلَ has no اِ in front — its hamzah drops out.

**Turning down more food takes the right sentence.** لَا شُكْرًا will be taken as mere politeness, and the offer repeated. What actually works: شَبِعْتُ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. It closes the offer warmly, not coldly.
**بِإِذْنِكُمْ — the polite way to take your leave.** Literally "with your permission". Leaving without it feels abrupt. The reply: تَفَضَّلْ or مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.

grammars.title: Accepting and declining invitations
after: In the Arab world, turning down a dinner invitation weighs more than in many Western cultures, so a refusal almost always comes with a **reason** and **an offer of another time**. Declining without both can read as keeping your distance.

grammars.title: Paired phrases you must know
after: If you only have time to memorize one thing from this unit, memorize this table. It's used many times a day across the Arab world, and answering with the right reply instantly marks you as someone who understands — far more than perfect grammar does.

blocks.title: Three things to know before you visit
items: **Bring something, however small.** Pastries, fruit, or a little gift from your country. Arriving empty-handed isn't forbidden, but bringing something is a language understood everywhere.
**Praise the home, but add مَا شَاءَ اللهُ.** Lavish praise without it can feel like casting the evil eye (اَلْعَيْن), and some people take this quite seriously.
**Don't rush off after the meal.** In many homes, tea or coffee after dinner is the most important part of the visit — that's when the real conversation happens.

Meaning
rows: May every year find you well
May it be your turn next

blocks.text: عُقْبَالَكَ is a distinctive, much-loved phrase: you say it to someone who hasn't yet had the good thing being celebrated — for example, to an unmarried guest at a wedding. It means roughly "may your turn come soon".

exercises.prompt: Write the right reply to each phrase.
Accept or decline each invitation in a complete sentence.
items: You're invited to dinner tomorrow: accept warmly.
You're invited but have an exam: decline with a reason.
You're asked out for the weekend: not sure yet.
You're invited to a friend's wedding: accept formally.
You're offered more food but you're full: decline properly.

exercises.prompt: Write ten sentences: you visit a friend's home, from arriving to leaving.

answers: اَلْعَفْوُ — اَللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ — اَللهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ — وَأَنْتَ بِخَيْرٍ — اَللهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ — مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ
شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَةِ. — بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا، مَا شَاءَ اللهُ. — اَلطَّعَامُ لَذِيذٌ جِدًّا. — شَبِعْتُ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. — هَلْ أُسَاعِدُكِ؟ — بِإِذْنِكُمْ.

بِكُلِّ سُرُورٍ، سَآتِي! — أَعْتَذِرُ، عِنْدِي اِمْتِحَانٌ غَدًا. رُبَّمَا الْمَرَّةَ الْقَادِمَةَ. — سَأُحَاوِلُ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ. — يُشَرِّفُنِي، شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَةِ. — شَبِعْتُ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. كُلُّ شَيْءٍ كَانَ مُمْتَازًا.

Example: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ! أَهْلًا بِكُمْ — هٰذِهِ هَدِيَّةٌ بَسِيطَةٌ مِنْ إِنْدُونِيسِيَا — بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا، مَا شَاءَ اللهُ — اَلطَّعَامُ لَذِيذٌ، يَدَاكِ سَلِيمَتَانِ — شَبِعْتُ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ — بِإِذْنِكُمْ، إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ
wave: Memorize this unit's table of paired phrases until the replies come out without thinking. It's the part of the language that pays off fastest.
